records.move: from Citibank Quito founding manager and Banco del Azuay manager to delegate and member of the Monetary Board at the Banco Central del Ecuador (1981), then to the board of Produbanco (Banco de la Produccion S.A.) from 2014
records.summary: Produbanco's own curriculum vitae for its board member lists, among his posts, 'Banco Central del Ecuador. Delegado-Vocal de la Junta Monetaria' in 1981, and his service as director and board member of Banco de la Produccion S.A. Produbanco from 2014 onwards. The same CV lists earlier private-bank posts at Citibank Quito, Banco del Pichincha, Banco del Azuay, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce and BAC Corp Securities. Produbanco's 2023 annual report describes the bank as 'el unico banco de capital privado en Latinoamerica'.

records.people: Saleh Ahmed Keshlaf (Central Bank of Libya from 1985; Director of the Governor's Office 1999-2012 and again from 2024)
records.move: from Director of the Governor's Office at the Central Bank of Libya (1999-2012) to bank board seats: board member of Arab Italian Bank (UBAE) 2005-2012, member of the Libyan Foreign Bank Supervisory Committee 2007-2012, Deputy Chairman of the Libyan Financial Services Company 2009-2024 and supervisory committee member of Joumhourria Bank 2012-2022
records.summary: A&T Bank's own board biography gives a full dated career: he began at the Central Bank of Libya's Research Department in 1985, was Director of the Governor's Office there from 1999 to 2012, advised its research and statistics department 2012-2024, and was reappointed Director of the Governor's Office in 2024. Alongside this it lists board or supervisory seats at Arab Italian Bank (UBAE), the Libyan Foreign Bank, the Libyan Financial Services Company and Joumhourria Bank. The page states no ownership for any of those firms, and the Libyan Foreign Bank and Joumhourria Bank are state institutions, so the move is filed as a public-sector move and is not counted.

MWI Federal Reserve gold: Reserve Bank of Malawi document list walked; read the Consolidated and Separate Annual Financial Statements for 2024 (ContentID 61585) and 2025 (63591) and the Report and Accounts for 2023 (59843), 2024 (61649) and 2025 (63680). All five carry the identical sentence 'The Bank holds monetary gold on deposit with the Federal Reserve Bank' with NO city, NO named Reserve Bank and NO custody or earmarking language. 'New York' appears in these documents only as 'Citibank New York'; the counterparty concentration tables list 'Federal Reserve Bank / United States of America / AAA' for cash and securities, not for gold. The 2021 statements (55391) contain no gold at all (RBM's gold holding is recent, 12,836.998 oz unchanged 2023-2025). The 2016-2020 and 2023 PDFs (36538, 23991, 12048, 46254, 55428, 58692) are scanned images with no extractable text. Neither (a) which Reserve Bank nor (b) custody-versus-placement is settled; stays off the map.

BOL Banco de Cochabamba: ASFI Memoria 1998 lists 'Banco de Cochabamba S.A.' only under 'Entidades en Liquidacion', the same status-not-ownership listing as the 1999 memoria. ASFI's 'Breve Resena de la Regulacion y Supervision Financiera en el Bicentenario de Bolivia' mentions it once, as 'la liquidacion del Banco Sur y Banco Cochabamba en 1995', with no ownership category. Neither document names Compania Boliviana de Seguros. Jaime Valencia Valencia's two employers remain UNSETTLED.

SDN National Bank / Workers National Bank: the Library of Congress Sudan country study (countrystudies.us/sudan/62.htm) says that after the 1970 Nationalization of Banks Act 'all domestic banks have been controlled by the Bank of Sudan' - control, not ownership - and names no 'National Bank' other than the National Bank of Egypt and no Workers National Bank. The Central Bank of Sudan's own financial institutions book (financial_inst_book_03.pdf) names neither bank; it lists nine banks in the central bank's participation-certificate fund (Bank of the Two Niles, Khartoum Bank, Sudanese Real Estate Bank, Faisal Islamic, Gharb Islamic, Sudanese French, Ivory, Animal Wealth, Mazaree' Commercial) without per-bank ownership. Wikipedia's 'National Bank of Sudan' page says 'The bank was established in 1981 by a group of Sudanese businessmen' and types it a private company (Bank Audi 75% from 2006) - but that founding year does not match Nimir's 1980-1982 dates and it is a weak source. Both employers remain UNSETTLED.

ECU Produbanco board CVs: Gustavo Francisco Vasconez Espinosa - no central bank post (closest is Banco del Estado, 1999, a state bank). Pablo Mauricio Arguello Godoy - no central bank post; career is Lloyds TSB Bank Plc 1991-2010 then Banco Promerica and Produbanco. Juan Diego Mosquera Pesantes - HIT, filed as a record. Hector Roberto Neira Calderon - no central bank post.

MRT Mohamed Cheikh El Kebir (Moulaye Taher), governor of the Banque Centrale de Mauritanie from 21 January 2020: financialafrik gives a full career inside the BCM (head of studies and visas, deputy director of economic studies, director for balance of payments and debt, director general for markets and liquidity from 2009, deputy governor 2014-2019) plus minister of employment 2007-2008 and minister of economy and industry from August 2019 - and one non-state employer, 'Caisses populaires d'epargne et de credit (PROCAPEC)', as managing director. The article states no ownership for PROCAPEC, so it does not count; the ministerial legs are public and the minister-of-economy leg is already on the map.

STP Americo d'Oliveira dos Ramos, new governor of the Banco Central de Sao Tome e Principe: the Forbes Africa Lusofona item names only 'ministro das Financas do Governo de Patrice Trovoada entre 2014 e 2018' - no bank, no BISTP. Already on the map as a public move.

HTI Sogebank Annual Report 2023-2024: the full conseil d'administration (Robert Moscoso, Raymond Jaar, Gladys M. Coupet, Dominique Bonnefil, Michel Theard, Claude Apaid, John Victor Handal, Joan Perry, Pierre-Marie Boisson, Franck Lanoix, Gaelle Riviere Wulff) and 22 senior managers are listed with titles only - no biographies, no BRH post, and the report states no shareholding structure.

MDG BNI Madagascar Annual Report 2020: board and executives listed with titles only, no biographies and no Banque Centrale de Madagascar post; two Treasury officials sit on it (Secretary General of the Government, Chief of Staff to the Director General of the Treasury), which are government, not central bank, posts. The report does state ownership - Indian Ocean Financial Holdings holds 51%, with CIEL Finance 58.43% and AXIAN Financial Services 41.57% of IOFHL, alongside the Malagasy State and staff - so BNI's mixed/private ownership is now on record for any future BNI lead.

DOM elDinero's item on the swearing-in of four new Junta Monetaria members (Arturo Martinez Moya, Eduardo de Jesus Tejera Curbelo, Sergia Elena Mejia de Seliman, Julio Cesar Llibre Salcedo) gives no employment history for any of them and names no private firm.
